To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LipL32/ 1 and LipL2/2 gene are the major outer membrane proteins of Leptospirae and the rLipL32/ 2 gene is a genus specific antigen.
the two recombinant proteins could induce antibodies against the 17 strains tested, and that the antibodies could block adherence of leptospires.
the LipL32/ 1 or LipL 32/ 2 gene of leptospira is a genus-specific antigenic determinant and can induce cross agglutinins and adherence blocking antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the construction and identification of the recombinations of the LipL 32 gene from the 17 dominant serogroups in China, and the recombinations could be applied as the diagnostic antigens for leptospirosis.
the existence, sequence, expression and immunity of rMOMP in leptospira.
the construction of expression systems and immunological identification for the two rMOMP1 (LipL 32/1) and rMOMP (LipL-32/2) of leptospira.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LipL32 gene and rMOMP1 or rMOMP2 can be used to develop a genus-specific diagnostic kit and vaccine against leptospirosis.
rMOMP1 or rMOMP2 may be the ideal candidate for the vaccine of leptospirosis.
rMOMP1 could be used as a genus-specific antigen of leptospira, and rMOMP1 or rMOMP2 as a vaccine candidate of leptospira.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LipL32 gene is a potential candidate for leptospira vaccine.
the two expression systems of rMOMP and the rabbit antisera against rMOMP1 or rMOMP2 are available to be used for immunodiagnosis and vaccine production of leptospirosis.
LipL32 gene could be divided into 2 genotypes LipL3/1 and Lip32/2, and the 2 genotypes of LipL32/ 1 and LipL3/2 gene could be used as genus-specific protein antigents of leptospira.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two rMOMP1s and rMOMP1 could be used to produce leptospirosis vaccines.
rMOMP1 could be used as a genus-specific antigen of leptospira.
LipL32 is a genus specific antigen of leptospira which could be used for serodiagnosis, and the expression systems constructed can be used for the development of the leptospira vaccine.
